claim: Every template wraps the attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` already exists on .NET Framework 4.0+ and in netstandard2.0, with class targets allowed. So projects targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework, a very common setup for MessagePack libraries, still get undecorated formatters and resolvers. The requirement asks for all generated code to be decorated. The derived criterion only allows conditional emission where the attribute does not exist, and ledger L7 defers to the requirement.

claim: The generated files now contain `#if` / `#endif` preprocessor lines that start at column 0 inside nested namespace or type emission. In the formatter, enum, union and string-key templates the `#if` lines sit directly after emitted nesting content, so any template that emits no preceding newline could place `#if` mid-line and break compilation. In FormatterTemplate.cs the `this.Write("#if ...` follows `this.Write("\r\n")`, so it is fine there. In StringKeyFormatterTemplate.cs and UnionTemplate.cs the previous write is the nesting-emitter output with no explicit newline, so the `#if` could be glued onto the end of the previous line, such as an opening `{` of a nested type or namespace. Preprocessor directives must be the first token on their line.
